finding.claim: With the default config (embed.allowed_domains = []), the Embed extension never installs DomainFilteringAdapter, so any https URL on its own line in untrusted Markdown is fetched server-side by the embed adapter (SSRF). Response-derived HTML is echoed back into the rendered output.
finding.source: Untrusted Markdown: a paragraph-free line consisting only of an https:// URL (src/Extension/Embed/EmbedStartParser.php:34-51, LinkParserHelper::parseLinkDestination).
finding.sink: src/Extension/Embed/Bridge/OscaroteroEmbedAdapter.php:43 $this->embedLib->getMulti(...) performs the outbound HTTP request; OscaroteroEmbedAdapter.php:46 copies the fetched code->html into the Embed node, which EmbedRenderer.php:33 returns unescaped.

trace.note: Only requires the line to start with 'https://' and be a single link destination.
Every top-level Embed node is passed to adapter->updateEmbeds().
DomainFilteringAdapter is only wrapped when allowed_domains !== []; with the default, the adapter is used unfiltered.
Outbound fetch of the attacker-supplied URL.
Fetched HTML stored on the node and rendered.

finding.guards_checked: Scheme: only https:// is accepted by the start parser, which does not stop internal HTTPS hosts. Host allowlist: DomainFilteringAdapter.php:47-60 is correct (scheme check, host from parse_url, exact or dot-suffix match), but it is not installed by default. No private/loopback/link-local/metadata IP blocking exists in this repo. Redirect handling and IP pinning are delegated to embed/embed, which is not vendored here, so unverified. Severity depends on the host app: it is a real SSRF only if the app uses the Embed extension without setting embed.allowed_domains. Reading the 'Repro' field: an app that renders untrusted Markdown with the Embed extension and default config; the attacker submits a line 'https://169.254.169.254/...' or an internal host URL. Whether internal response content is visible depends on embed/embed extracting it into code->html; this is unverified. Blind SSRF is still possible via timing or DNS callbacks.

finding.claim: Embed codes are fetched from remote sites and output verbatim, skipping the html_input/escape filtering that applies to raw HTML. If an allowed (or unrestricted) domain serves attacker-controlled oEmbed/og HTML that includes unescaped attacker values, that yields stored XSS in the rendering page even when html_input=escape is set.
finding.source: Remote HTTP response from a domain reachable by the attacker (any domain when allowed_domains is empty, or a user-generated-content domain on the allowlist). Entry: untrusted Markdown with a bare https:// URL line.
finding.sink: src/Extension/Embed/EmbedRenderer.php:33 returns $node->getEmbedCode() without HtmlFilter, and OscaroteroEmbedAdapter.php:46 stores extractor->code->html.

trace.note: Remote code->html assigned to the embed node.
Returned raw; not passed through HtmlFilter/html_input.

finding.guards_checked: html_input is applied only in HtmlBlockRenderer.php:44-46 and HtmlInlineRenderer.php:44-46, not to Embed nodes. There is no sanitizer for embed HTML. The exploit requires embed/embed to emit attacker-controlled, unescaped values into code->html, which I could not verify because the library is not vendored. Hence PLAUSIBLE, not CONFIRMED.
